subject: Phased commit credits, invoice cadence and reseller split
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@medsyn.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Phased commit: credit timing, invoice align & reseller split

Hi Diego / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. To summarize Medsyn's high level plan: we expect a 12-month private-offer commitment split across three phases (Q4 2025, Q1 2026, Q2 2026) with roughly 40/35/25 allocations. Procurement has two practical questions before we move to legal/DocuSign:

1) Credit timing: can the commit credits be applied pro-rata across the three invoices, or do credits need to land up-front on the first invoice? We need to understand how the marketplace private-offer crediting maps to our invoice cadence so our finance team can model cashflow.

2) Reseller pass-through: we work with CloudBridge (our reseller). How do you recommend the reseller split be handled operationally — is the reseller cut taken at invoice time (we receive a net invoice) or does Redwood issue the invoice at list and run a monthly settlement to the reseller? We need this detail to confirm our internal margin waterfall.

I've attached our current_commit_schedule.xlsx to show exact milestone dates. Can you send a short model showing the two crediting scenarios and the resulting net invoice amounts to CloudBridge? Also please confirm any additional evidence procurement will need to approve (tax certificates, reseller agreement references).

Best,
Elena
Director of Procurement
Medsyn Health

Attachments: current_commit_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@medsyn.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased commit: credit timing, invoice align & reseller split

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the schedule. High-level answers below, plus a quick workbook attached that models both options.

Option A — Up-front application:
- Redwood applies the majority of the private-offer credit on the first invoice generated via the marketplace.
- Pros: simpler from a settlement perspective, quicker visibility of net cost for CloudBridge and Medsyn.
- Cons: larger single-period accounting impact for your finance team; if you request net invoicing to Medsyn, that requires reseller-level settlement reconciliation afterward.

Option B — Phased/pro-rata application (recommended for your split):
- Credits are distributed across your committed phases (Q4/Q1/Q2) proportional to the committed amounts. Redwood will annotate each marketplace invoice with the applied credit line so procurement sees net unit price per invoice.
- Pros: smoother cashflow, aligns to how you plan to recognize consumption.
- Cons: requires monthly or quarterly settlement records for CloudBridge to reconcile their reseller margin (we can provide a monthly export).

Reseller mechanics (two practical paths):
1) Net invoice to you: Redwood pays CloudBridge their reseller margin in a separate settlement; Medsyn receives a single net invoice.
2) List invoice + separate settlement: Redwood invoices at list via the marketplace, then issues a monthly settlement to CloudBridge for their commission.

Operational recommendation for Medsyn + CloudBridge: choose Option B (phased credits) with Path 2 (list invoice + monthly settlement). That keeps marketplace records auditable, preserves list-price traceability for compliance, and lets CloudBridge receive a clear monthly settlement file. We can also produce a one-page settlement report that shows per-invoice credit applied, reseller commission, and net amounts.

I've attached a pricing_workbook.xlsx with two tabs — "Scenario_A_upfront" and "Scenario_B_phased" plus a "Modeling" tab for reseller splits. Please review and tell me which scenario your finance prefers; Ben, would appreciate any channel ops constraints before I send this to CloudBridge.

Thanks — I can also hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk the workbook.

— Diego
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_workbook.xlsx (model stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@medsyn.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Oct 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased commit: credit timing, invoice align & reseller split

Looping in a couple of operational notes from channel side:

- For CloudBridge we typically recommend the list-invoice + monthly settlement approach when deals have phased commits — it preserves eligibility tracking for partner incentives and reduces disputes at the customer-facing invoice.

- Suggested reseller split mechanics for modeling: 1) apply a 10% reseller commission on the list price at invoice run; 2) on true-up/phase 2–3 invoices, reduce the commission to 5% for incremental usage above the first phase (this accounts for their initial enablement work). These percentages are configurable; I've included them in the "Modeling" tab of the workbook.

- Tax handling: if Medsyn wants net invoicing semantics, we'll need a reseller exemption / reseller invoicing addendum signed by CloudBridge. Otherwise, the settlement file shows gross list, reseller commission, and Redwood remittance to CloudBridge.

Operational ask: Diego, can you include a short CSV export sample in the workbook that shows the monthly settlement fields (invoice_id, invoice_date, list_amount, credit_applied, reseller_commission, net_due_to_customer, remittance_date)? Elena — that CSV is what CloudBridge asked to ingest.

Ben
Sr. Channel Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

If you can get the CSV sample + the one-page addendum and the DocuSign link to me by end of day Friday (03 Oct), procurement can route to legal and we'll aim to sign within a week. Once signed we'll notify CloudBridge to expect the settlement files.
